newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Philippines' Estrada fails to meet Saudi officials.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Estrada fails to meet Saudi officials.

text.p: Philippines Vice-President Joseph Estrada has failed to meet Saudi officials to discuss around 200 jailed Filipino workers during his three-day visit to the kingdom, a Filipino official said on Sunday.
"Estrada was not able to meet any Saudi officials to request clemency for jailed Filipino workers," Estrada's communications director Reli German told Reuters.
Estrada was to see Saudi Crown Prince Abdullah on Saturday morning, but the meeting was cancelled, German said without elaborating.
German said a formal letter from Philippines President Fidel Ramos to Prince Abdullah had been left with the ambassador in Riyadh to deliver.
Another Filipino official travelling with Estrada told Reuters there were 34 Filipina workers among the 200 jailed. The charges against those in jail were not provided.
However, Estrada had said he wanted to discuss those facing death sentences. Official sources said 33 Filipinos were awaiting execution, most for murder and drugs charges.
The sources said 16 Filipinos were arrested last month in Riyadh for staging a protest outside the Philippines embassy.
There are about four million Filipinos working overseas, many in the Gulf. Around half a million Filipinos work in Saudi Arabia alone.
Estrada arrived in Bahrain from Saudi Arabia on Saturday evening for a two-day official visit. He was due to fly to Rome later on Sunday.
